{{Short description|Acceptance Sampling Technique}}

In [[statistics]], a '''variables sampling plan''' is an [[acceptance sampling]] technique. Plans for [[Variable_(mathematics)|variables]] are intended for quality characteristics that are measured on a continuous scale. This plan requires the knowledge of the [[statistical model]] (e.g. [[normal distribution]]). The historical [[Evolution of mathematics|evolution]] of this technique dates back to the seminal work of [[W. Allen Wallis]] (1943). The purpose of a plan for variables is to assess whether the process is operating far enough from the specification limit. Plans for variables may produce a similar OC curve to attribute plans with significantly less sample size.

The decision criterion of these plans are 
:<math> \bar{X}+ k\sigma \leqslant USL </math> or <math> \bar{X}- k\sigma \geqslant LSL </math>
where <math>\bar{X}</math> and <math>\sigma</math> are the [[sample mean]] and the [[standard deviation]] respectively, <math>k</math> is the [[critical distance]], <math>USL</math> and <math>LSL</math> are the upper and lower regulatory limits. When the above expression is satisfied the proportion nonconforming is lower than expected and therefore the lot is accepted.

A variables sampling plan can be designed so that the OC curve passes through two points (AQL,<math>\alpha</math>) and (LQL,<math>\beta</math>). AQL and LQL are the [[Acceptable quality limit]] and the limiting quality level respectively. <math>\alpha</math> and <math>\beta</math> are the producer and consumer's risks. The required [[Sample size determination|sample size]] (<math>n</math>) and the critical distance (<math>k</math>) can be obtained as
:<math> k = \frac{Z_{LQL}Z_{\alpha}+Z_{AQL}Z_{\beta}}{Z_{\alpha}+Z_{\beta}} </math>
where <math>Z</math> is the [[normal distribution]] function.

When the [[Dispersion (statistics)|dispersion]] is known the required sample size (<math>n</math>) is obtained from 
:<math> n = \left ( \frac{Z_\alpha +Z_\beta}{Z_{AQL}-Z_{LQL}}\right )^{2} </math>

while for unknown <math>\sigma</math> the sample size is approximately 
:<math> n = \left ( \frac{Z_\alpha+Z_\beta}{Z_{AQL}-Z_{LQL}}\right )^{2}\left ( 1+\frac{k^2}{2} \right ) </math>

The [[iarchive:MIL-STD-414|MIL-STD-414]] provides tables to obtain the required sample size and the critical distance according to the type of inspection.
